Consumer Non-Cyclicals: The Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 34.85%, placing it tenth out of fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Its average annual revenue grew by 8.97%, which ranks the sector sixth among its peers for revenue growth. [#VC2.SI]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2.SI] delivered the strongest earnings increase within the sector, while [#EB5.SI]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5.SI] achieved the highest revenue growth. In Singapore, the sector benefits from a steady demand for essential household goods, a regulatory focus on food security, and a consumer base that prioritises price‑stable staples, all of which uniquely support its performance. These sector‑specific dynamics, combined with the strong company‑level drivers, underpin the robust growth observed over the past year.
Consumer Cyclicals: Despite a modest decline in earnings, the Consumer Cyclicals sector posted an average annual earnings growth of minus 7.3% over the past year, placing it 14th out of 15 sectors for earnings growth. In contrast, revenue expanded by 14.13% on average, earning the sector the third-best rank among all sectors for revenue growth. The strongest earnings performer was [#AWK.SI]Fuxing China Group Ltd[\#AWK.SI], while [#5HH.SI]Prospera Global Ltd[\#5HH.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. Growth in Singapore is shaped by local consumer confidence, which is sensitive to fluctuations in disposable income and the pace of tourism recovery, as well as seasonal demand spikes around major festivals and the impact of recent changes to import duties on luxury goods. These Singapore-specific dynamics help explain why revenue can rise sharply even when earnings lag behind.
Transportation & Logistics: The Transportation & Logistics sector posted modest earnings growth of 1.88% on average over the past year, while revenue expanded by 2.71%. Among the fifteen SGX sectors, it ranked thirteenth for earnings growth and also thirteenth for revenue growth. [#R14.SI]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14.SI] led the sector with the strongest yearly earnings increase, whereas [#FQ7.SI]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7.SI] recorded the highest revenue growth. Growth in the sector is shaped by Singapore’s limited port berth availability, which pressures operators to improve turnaround efficiency, and by ongoing government initiatives to digitise freight handling and integrate multimodal logistics platforms. Additionally, tighter work‑pass regulations have increased labor costs, and the surge in e‑commerce demand continues to drive higher parcel volumes across the island.
Healthcare: Over the past year the Healthcare sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 26.57%, while average revenue grew by 3.87%. This earnings expansion ranks the sector 11th out of 15 sectors, and its revenue growth places it 10th. The strongest earnings performance came from [#FHH.SI]FHH[\#FHH.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings increase within the sector, and [#8YY.SI]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY.SI] led revenue growth. Growth is further supported by Singapore’s ageing demographic, which drives higher demand for chronic disease management and elder-care services. In addition, recent expansions of public health initiatives and increased reimbursement rates for locally produced medical devices have uniquely boosted sector performance. These factors together help explain the robust earnings growth despite modest revenue expansion.
Properties & Real Estate: Properties & Real Estate posted an average annual earnings growth of about 88.46%, placing it third among the fifteen SGX sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at an average annual rate of roughly 11.81%, earning the sector a fourth‑place ranking for top‑line growth. The strongest drivers came from [#5IC.SI][#5IC.SI]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC.SI][\#5IC.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings increase and also led the sector in revenue growth. Growth in the sector is further shaped by Singapore’s scarce land supply and ongoing government policies that tighten loan‑to‑value ratios and impose additional stamp duties on foreign buyers, which together modulate demand and pricing dynamics. At the same time, strong demand for logistics space linked to the island’s status as a regional hub continues to support rental yields and property valuations.
Energy: The Energy sector posted a robust earnings expansion of 48.84% on average, placing it seventh out of fifteen sectors for earnings growth, while its average revenue rose 21.13%, earning the top rank for revenue growth among all sectors. [#JFQ.SI]JFQ[\#JFQ.SI] delivered the strongest yearly earnings increase within the sector, and [#TPED.SI]PTT Exploration Production PCL DRC[\#TPED.SI] recorded the highest yearly revenue growth. Growth has been further fueled by Singapore’s role as a regional hub for oil refining and storage, recent expansions in LNG import and re‑export capacity, and government incentives that encourage investment in both traditional and cleaner energy projects, all of which uniquely support the sector’s performance in the local market.
Utilities: Despite a sharp contraction in revenue, the Utilities sector posted an average annual earnings growth of about 45.5%, placing it eighth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue fell by roughly 5.4% on average, which is the weakest performance across all sectors, ranking fifteenth. The sector’s earnings boost is driven in part by [#5GD.SI]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth among its peers. Conversely, [#BEH.SI]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH.SI] delivered the strongest revenue increase despite the overall decline. In Singapore, the utilities outlook is shaped by regulatory tariff reviews, the need to integrate more renewable capacity into a grid that was historically dominated by thermal generation, and the impact of fuel import cost volatility, all of which uniquely influence the sector’s growth dynamics.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 50.54% over the past year, while revenue rose by 10.8%. This earnings performance places the sector sixth out of fifteen sectors, and its revenue growth ranks it fifth among the same group. [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion in the sector, and [#42W.SI]Zixin Group Holdings Ltd[\#42W.SI] recorded the highest revenue increase. Growth has been further supported by Singapore’s high household savings rate and government initiatives that encourage local sourcing of essential goods, which together sustain demand for everyday consumer products despite broader market fluctuations.
Financial Services: The Financial Services sector recorded modest earnings growth of 1.91% while revenue expanded by 7.73% over the past year. Among fifteen SGX sectors, it ranked twelfth for earnings growth and eighth for revenue growth. [#I49.SI]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49.SI] delivered the strongest earnings increase in the sector, and [#U13.SI]United Overseas Insurance Ltd[\#U13.SI] posted the highest revenue growth. Growth was shaped by Singapore's tight regulatory framework that encourages capital adequacy, the continued shift toward digital banking, and rising demand for insurance products as the population ages. These sector‑specific dynamics helped lift revenue despite the relatively low earnings acceleration.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector posted a steep decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings growth of -109.07%, placing it at the bottom of all fifteen sectors. Despite the earnings contraction, revenue grew modestly by 3.4% on average, earning the sector the eleventh spot in revenue growth rankings among the fifteen sectors. [#9VW.SI][#9VW.SI]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW.SI][\#9VW.SI] stood out as the top performer, delivering the highest earnings growth and also leading revenue growth within the sector. The sector’s performance is shaped by Singapore’s tightly regulated broadcast and telecom licensing framework, which limits new entrants and can suppress profit margins, while the nation’s high broadband penetration and government initiatives to expand digital content create incremental revenue opportunities. Consequently, earnings remain under pressure even as modest revenue gains reflect the ongoing shift toward digital consumption.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector posted an extraordinary earnings surge, with an average annual earnings growth of 993.54%, placing it first among the fifteen SGX sectors. Revenue grew more modestly at an average annual rate of 8.49%, earning the sector a seventh‑place ranking for revenue growth. [#KUO.SI]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO.SI] drove the earnings outperformance, while [#C8R.SI]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R.SI] led the revenue expansion. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s ongoing infrastructure upgrades, which increase demand for cement and construction inputs, and by regional export pipelines that benefit chemical producers facing limited domestic raw material supplies. These sector‑specific dynamics helped sustain the strong performance despite broader market conditions.
Infrastructures: With an average annual earnings growth of roughly 297%, the Infrastructures sector outpaces almost all peers, ranking second in earnings growth among fifteen sectors. Revenue, however, expands more modestly at about 2.9% per year, placing the sector twelfth for revenue growth. The strongest earnings surge comes from [#Z74.SI]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z74.SI], while [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI] leads the revenue gains. Growth is driven by Singapore’s continued investment in expanding broadband networks and upgrading airport maintenance capabilities, both of which are core to the nation’s position as a regional hub. These sector‑specific projects fuel the earnings surge while keeping overall revenue expansion modest.
REIT: The REIT sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 38.88% over the past year, placing it ninth among fifteen sectors for earnings growth. Its average annual revenue grew by 4.52%, also ranking ninth out of fifteen sectors for revenue growth. [#M1GU.SI]Alpha Integrated REIT[\#M1GU.SI] led the sector with the strongest earnings expansion, while [#DCRU.SI]Digital Core REIT[\#DCRU.SI] recorded the highest revenue increase. Growth in the sector is shaped by Singapore’s limited land supply, which fuels demand for high‑quality, income‑generating properties, and by the regulatory framework that encourages REIT listings and stable dividend policies. The expanding logistics hub network and rising demand for data centre space further support rental growth, while a low interest rate environment influences yield compression and asset valuations.
Industrials: The Industrials sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 68.46%, placing it fourth out of fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. In contrast, its average annual revenue growth was modest at 2.08%, resulting in a fourteenth place ranking for revenue growth. Within the sector, [#5OC.SI]Koyo International Ltd[\#5OC.SI] delivered the strongest yearly earnings increase, while [#Y06.SI]Green Build Technology Ltd[\#Y06.SI] led the revenue surge. Growth has been reinforced by Singapore’s ongoing expansion of port facilities and the government’s commitment to upgrading transport networks, which create steady demand for engineering and construction services. At the same time, tighter capacity constraints in local logistics and a shift toward sustainable building practices have added pressure on revenue generation, tempering the sector’s overall revenue growth.
Technology: The Technology sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 54.13%, the highest among its peers. It ranks fifth in earnings growth out of fifteen sectors, while its revenue growth of 16.28% places it second in the revenue growth ranking. Within the sector, [#5AB.SI]Trek 2000 International Ltd[\#5AB.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion, and [#9MT.SI]MetaOptics Ltd[\#9MT.SI] led the revenue surge. Growth has been amplified by Singapore’s aggressive push for smart city initiatives, extensive high speed broadband rollout, and generous government grants for semiconductor and photonics research, all of which have heightened demand for technology products. These sector‑specific factors have helped sustain the strong earnings and revenue momentum.
